Florida's locally acquired dengue cases nearly doubled in one week, adding 32 new cases and prompting aerial spraying in Tampa Bay areas. In Bangladesh, dengue infections surged sharply in Chattogram, with over 500 cases recorded in the first week of September amid persistent rains.
An 80-year-old woman in Tampa, Florida, died from dengue fever, marking a severe outcome in the local outbreak. In Bangladesh, three more dengue-related deaths and 1,463 new hospitalizations were reported in the past 24 hours, continuing the country's ongoing outbreak.

incidents.summary: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has spread to a seventh province, South-Ubangi, and confirmed cases have now surpassed 7,000, with over 3,300 deaths reported as of early September. Africa's top health body warns the virus is rapidly spreading beyond its epicenter in eastern Congo, threatening neighboring nations. Meanwhile, one report indicates a slight downward trend in cases, though the peak has not yet been confirmed.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. logs.summary: The selected news reports widespread drought impacts globally. In the U.S., Lake Powell hit a record low, and Amarillo entered Stage 1 drought contingency. The UK saw Wessex Water impose its first hosepipe ban since 1976, and drought worsened in southern Queensland, Australia. Germany's Rhine River remained low, threatening navigation, and the NFU warned of crop failures. Other reports highlighted severe drought in Wisconsin, reduced grain harvests in Germany, and the potential for a super El Niño affecting Latin America and Sri Lanka.

logs.summary:
New reports indicate drought worsening in several regions: Norfolk and Virginia Beach issued Condition II drought notifications urging water conservation, while Halifax County, Virginia restricted bulk water hauling due to extreme drought. Benton County, Arkansas reached exceptional drought status for the first time since 2012. In contrast, Amarillo lifted its Stage 1 drought contingency plan. The U.S. Small Business Administration approved disaster loans for eight southeast Colorado counties. Internationally, 218 districts in India face drought-like conditions, and severe drought in Angola is driving communities to migrate to Namibia. Additionally, Idaho and South Dakota report increased human-wildlife conflicts and drying wells, respectively.
New reports detail drought conditions worsening in Virginia, with Norfolk and Virginia Beach issuing Condition II drought notifications urging water conservation. In Minnesota, severe drought is expected to mute fall colors and cause early leaf drop, while in Kansas, heat and drought are taking a toll on corn and soybean crops. Additionally, forecasts confirm a near-certain super El Niño that may be the strongest on record, with maps showing potential for extreme drought in some regions.

Survivors face water shortages, and international aid and domestic relief efforts are underway.

logs.summary:
As of September 9, the death toll from the June 24 twin earthquakes has risen to at least 6,500, according to reports highlighting how Venezuelans in the U.S. continue to grieve for lost loved ones and contribute to recovery efforts.
A new report reveals that the FAA's UTM drone coordination system failed during the earthquake response because it requires intact cellular networks, a structural gap that affected airspace management despite drones saving over 6,600 lives. Atlas Insurance employees raised funds to support relief efforts through SOS Malta, adding to ongoing international private sector contributions.

news.headline: How Organized Communities Are Rebuilding in the Wake of Venezuela’s Twin Earthquakes
news.body: At 3:55 a.m. on June 25, a flicker of cellular service allowed Carlos to send word to the outside world from the rubble of his home in La Guaira that he and his family had survived the twin earthquakes that shook Venezuela’s capital region hours earlier. “For now, I’m in a makeshift shelter near where my house used to be,” he wrote. “We’re trying to help and rescue our neighbors.” Then the service went out again. In the days that followed, Carlos, his neighbors, state workers, and thousands of Venezuelans dug through rubble and what remained of their homes to pull out their family, friends, and neighbors – both those who survived, and those who did not (6,462 and 6,509 respectively, according to latest official figures). Thousands more sought refuge where they could, with the largest shelter, Caribbean Maritime University, reporting an estimated 4,000 or more people in the early days (down to 2,600 within a week as other shelters were set up to provide more dignified conditions or as survivors found other housing solutions, and 830 as of late August).

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

news.headline: Europe's hot, dry summer takes its toll with fires in France and Greece, and drought in the UK
news.body: Europe is grappling with a record-breaking hot and dry summer. Water-dropping planes on Monday tackled a major wildfire in Greece while firefighters in France worked to stabilize a blaze in Provence. The United Kingdom recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Strong winds returned in Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway. In France, firefighters guarded against flare-ups near Bordeaux. The U.K. weather service reported a prolonged heat wave and lack of rainfall. Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.

news.headline: Europe Battles Extreme Weather: France, Spain, Serbia & Bosnia Hit By Wildfires, Floods And Storms
news.body: Extreme weather is gripping multiple European nations as severe wildfires, flash floods and powerful storms force thousands of people to evacuate. France is battling a major wildfire across the Cap Ferret Peninsula in the southwest, where extreme summer heat and months of drought have created dangerous fire conditions. Authorities ordered the evacuation of the popular tourism hotspot as flames threatened homes and the peninsula’s main escape route. More than 10,000 hectares of forest have reportedly been affected, while around 63,000 people, including large numbers of tourists, were forced to leave the area. Boats and emergency teams were deployed as authorities worked to protect residents and visitors. Spain is also facing a contrasting weather crisis, with intense wildfires occurring alongside torrential rainfall and flash flooding. Heavy rains disrupted road and rail transport and injured more than 11 people.

Rain on August 17 brought some relief, slowing the fire's advance towards the German border.

logs.summary: Severe monsoon rains and cyclones have caused widespread flooding across the Philippines, particularly in Luzon, with damage nearing P4 billion in Central Luzon and P2.68 billion in infrastructure damage in the Ilocos Region, affecting over four million people. At least two brothers drowned in a submerged bypass road in Pampanga, and a baby was dramatically rescued from flash floods in Manila. In response, lawmakers are pushing for flood control master plan reviews and Senate investigations into the government's disaster response.

logs.summary:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council reported 43 deaths attributed to the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng, and Pilandok. Flooding persisted in 385 areas in Luzon that received above-average rainfall, while PAGASA warned that heavy monsoon rain could trigger floods in four provinces, with Zambales likely to be most affected in the next 24 hours.
San Lazaro Hospital in Manila reported 22 leptospirosis deaths as of Sept. 7, while Quezon City exceeded the epidemic threshold for the disease following heavy rains. Agricultural losses from the southwest monsoon flooding have reached at least P3.62 billion. Meanwhile, the NBI may summon Rep. Paolo Duterte over nearly P1.9 billion in flood control projects in Davao City awarded to a single contractor.

news.headline: Indonesia Cancels Flights at Jakarta Airport, Others as Anak Krakatau Volcano Erupts
news.body: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau volcano erupted early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic ash drifted across parts of western Indonesia. Indonesia’s Geological Agency said the volcanic island located in Indonesia’s Sunda Strait between the main Java and Sumatra islands had showed signs of activity since Friday before erupting for 30 seconds at 3:53 a.m. Sunday. Closed-circuit camera footage showed lava flares from the volcano.

logs.summary:
As of September 10, rescuers continued searching for a speedboat carrying eight people—five journalists, two crew, and a guide—who went missing on September 9 while heading to Anak Krakatau to report on the eruption, after the search was previously paused due to high waves and poor visibility. Meanwhile, Anak Krakatau's intermittent eruption persisted, with officials noting it remained ongoing days after the initial activity.
Up to 200 Hong Kong-bound domestic helpers remain stranded in Indonesia due to the ongoing Anak Krakatau eruption, according to reports. Additionally, MetMalaysia has stated there are no indications of volcanic ash entering Malaysian airspace, easing earlier concerns about the ash plume spreading.

news.headline: MAMAMOO’s Concert In Jakarta Cancelled
news.body: MAMAMOO’s upcoming concert in Jakarta has been canceled. The group’s “4WARD” concert in Jakarta, which was scheduled to take place at NICE PIK 2 on September 19, 2026, has been canceled due to ongoing unpredictable circumstances following recent volcanic activity in Indonesia. Read RBW’s full statement below: Hello, this is RBW. We regret to inform you that the “MAMAMOO 2026 WORLD TOUR <4WARD> in JAKARTA,” which was scheduled to take place at NICE PIK 2 on September 19, 2026, has been canceled due to unavoidable circumstances. Due to recent volcanic activity in Indonesia, along with strengthened local safety and security measures, unpredictable circumstances have continued to develop. After discussions with the local promoter, we ultimately decided to cancel the concert with the safety of the artists and audience as our top priority. All tickets purchased will be fully refunded. Please refer to a separate announcement from the ticketing platform and local promoter for details regarding the refund process and schedule. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience and concern this cancellation may cause to the fans who have been looking forward to the concert, and we kindly ask for your understanding. Thank you.
